1644.x: The full series index and recommended reading order.

1645.t: Saga compensation and the reconciliation backstop
1645.x: Undo as a first-class event handler: give back stock a committed transaction already took, with a periodic sweep as the saga-timeout backstop.

1646.x: A shared OpenTelemetry baseline with CQRS duration metrics, correlation IDs, and outbox-poll span filtering, exported to Azure Monitor.

1647.t: Security headers and CSP for Blazor
1647.x: One middleware stamps hardened response headers on every host, with the Blazor CSP resolved through a pluggable provider.

1648.x: An AES-256-GCM value converter that keeps a PII column ciphertext even for someone who can query the database.

1649.t: Feature flags in the CQRS pipeline
1649.x: Gate commands and queries at the outermost decorator, so a handler never checks a flag and a disabled feature is rejected before any work runs.

1650.t: HTTP API versioning, proven not just claimed
1650.x: Header-based versioning introduced without breaking a single caller, plus a fitness contract that proves two live versions coexist.

1651.t: Managed file storage: uploads you don't have to trust
1651.x: Attacker-controlled bytes become safe avatars: content sniffing, metadata stripping, re-encoding, and pluggable blob storage.

1652.x: The same Blazor components run in a browser and inside a MAUI hybrid app; small per-capability contracts reach native hardware without ever asking 'am I on mobile?'.

1653.t: Two real apps on one framework
1653.x: A case study: a conference platform and an e-commerce store built on the same kernel.

1654.x: Author your first architecture fitness test and watch it fail the build on a violation.

1655.x: A hands-on walkthrough of building a new module across all five layers.

1656.t: i18n and theming on one preference pipeline
1656.x: A culture choice and a theme choice ride the same cookie, profile column, and login reconciliation: one persistence path, two switches.

1657.x: A shared Blazor and MudBlazor UI layer with accessibility enforced by axe in CI.

1658.t: Soft-delete vs the right to erasure
1658.x: Soft-delete for lifecycle, anonymization plus outbox purge for GDPR/CCPA erasure, and why both exist.

1659.x: How the framework's tests stack up: fast unit and architecture tests at the base, E2E at the tip.

1660.x: Architecture rules that fail the build: a compile-time layer guard plus a shared NetArchTest rule library.

1661.x: Standard resilience on every outbound client, plus declared RTO/RPO and a drilled restore.

1662.t: Extracting a module to a gRPC service
1662.x: A step-by-step extraction of an in-process module into its own gRPC service, database, and auth.

1663.x: Model services, databases, and the broker as one Aspire graph that runs from laptop to Azure with one command.

1664.x: Two layers that cover the whole API edge: endpoint rate limits plus lockout-based brute-force defense on identity.

1665.x: Beyond roles and permissions: which rows you may touch, enforced per resource.

1666.x: A write-once REST surface every entity inherits, plus a bounded dynamic query contract that is never open SQL.

1667.x: A short-lived JWT plus one server-stored refresh token that rotates on every use, with reuse detection that makes a stolen token end its own session.

1668.t: External OAuth login behind your own JWTs
1668.x: Sign in with Google or GitHub without leaking provider tokens: external identity exchanged for your own JWTs at the boundary.

1669.t: Browser session-cookie auth for Blazor SSR
1669.x: HttpOnly session cookies and an SSR-time scheme so [Authorize] passes during prerender, with the API still the boundary.

1670.x: A capability layer over RBAC: permission policies that resolve on demand from a central registry.

1671.x: Why source-generated, per-entity mappers beat reflection-based mapping for clarity and speed.

1672.t: Live channels over one SignalR hub
1672.x: Sub-second ephemeral events (polls, Q&A, live counts) fanned out over the existing notification hub, with nothing persisted.

1673.x: A notifications feature built as a clean vertical slice across every layer.

1674.t: Problem Details across HTTP and gRPC
1674.x: One error contract mapped consistently to HTTP Problem Details and gRPC status.

1675.x: A caching decorator where commands invalidate and queries populate, plus an authenticated output-cache tier at the API edge.

1676.x: Dedup client retries with an Idempotency-Key header and cached replay, plus a consumer-side inbox for brokers.

1677.x: The non-negotiables of password storage in .NET, done correctly and tested.

1678.x: Validate another service's RS256 tokens via JWKS discovery, with no shared secret crossing a boundary.

1679.x: Every integration event carries a schema version; breaking changes get a new event type and an upcaster, never a silent reshape.

1680.x: Modules declare their dependencies and load in topological order, so registration is never hand-sequenced.

1681.x: Carry the RowVersion from database to DTO and back, so a concurrent edit fails fast as a conflict instead of silently overwriting.

1682.x: Eager-load relationships that cross containers and data sources without N+1 or a leaky abstraction.

1683.t: Polyglot persistence: one model, three engines
1683.x: SQL Server, Cosmos, and SQLite behind a single entity model, with the engine chosen by attribute.

1684.x: Give each module its own database and outbox before you extract it, so extraction changes hosting, not data.

1685.x: Events that survive a crash: persist them atomically with your data, then dispatch at least once.

1686.x: A validation kit that composes FluentValidation rules instead of copy-pasting them across features.

1687.x: Thin command and query handlers wrapped by a Scrutor decorator chain whose order is load-bearing.

1688.x: Compose queries from reusable specification objects instead of scattering LINQ across handlers.

1689.x: Push behavior into rich aggregates with factory methods and invariants instead of bags of public setters.

1690.x: Model expected failures as Result values with a transport-agnostic error type, and keep exceptions for the genuinely exceptional.

1691.x: A two-axis rubric for scoring architecture on maturity and implementation, so 'good architecture' stops being a vibe.

1692.x: The cornerstone idea: build the monolith now and extract a service later with no rewrite, via module discovery, gRPC contracts, and a YARP gateway.

1693.x: Why I open-sourced a production .NET framework and scored it against a 34-category architecture rubric, gaps and all.
